questions.short_title: Stroke triage app adopted but not embedded
questions.question: The Stroke Triage App was well accepted, so what stopped it becoming routine practice?
options: Poor workflow fit and limited perceived added value
Technical failures and unreliable performance
No training or local champions to promote it
Doubts about the accuracy of its advice
questions.explanation: Adoption was good, but clinical urgency, poor workflow integration and limited perceived added value got in the way of routine use. Also, usage data can't show whether the app's advice actually changed triage decisions.

questions.short_title: Paediatric prehospital fentanyl: serious adverse effects rare
questions.question: What did this study find about serious opioid-related adverse effects in children given prehospital opioids?
options: Bradycardia and respiratory depression did not occur at all in the cohort
About 15% of children developed respiratory depression requiring naloxone
Serious adverse effects were rare but half the children received an opioid antidote
Bradycardia and respiratory depression each occurred in 0.7%, and no child needed an opioid antidote
questions.explanation: Serious signs were uncommon: bradycardia and respiratory depression each affected 0.7% of children, and no opioid antidote was given. Keep in mind the 15.1% with compatible signs were mostly nonspecific ones like nausea and drowsiness, which a retrospective register review can't firmly attribute to opioids.

questions.short_title: Mainstream and sidestream capnography give different ETCO2
questions.question: Mainstream capnography gave higher ETCO2 readings than sidestream during resuscitation, yet both devices agreed on what?
options: The timing of each chest compression
The overall trend of ETCO2 over time
Whether ETCO2 exceeded 45 mmHg
The ventilation rate needed for good CPR
questions.explanation: Despite mainstream readings running about 3.94 mmHg higher, both technologies tracked trends almost identically and flagged abrupt rises and drops together. With only 23 recordings, the wide limits of agreement are imprecisely estimated, so treat absolute values with caution depending on the device used.

questions.short_title: Community first responders trained but rarely dispatched
questions.question: Despite most registered community first responders feeling prepared to respond to a cardiac arrest, what did the survey reveal about their actual real-world experience?
options: Only 15.1% had ever been dispatched, and just 1.9% had actually performed CPR
Most had been dispatched, but nearly all arrived after EMS on scene
Over half had been dispatched at least once, but few felt confident responding
None had been dispatched, since they lived in regions without any alerting system
questions.explanation: Only 15.1% had ever been dispatched and 1.9% had performed CPR, even though 97.3% felt prepared. That confidence came from volunteers with almost no real dispatch experience, so it should be treated cautiously.

questions.short_title: Prehospital stroke triage: high under- and overtriage rates
questions.question: In the Lausanne stroke pathway study, what happened to EMS under- and overtriage rates when the coordinated medical team call step was added?
options: Both rates stayed roughly the same
Overtriage fell to zero while undertriage was unchanged
Both rates fell, with undertriage dropping from 21% to 11%
Undertriage fell but overtriage rose sharply
questions.explanation: The second expert assessment step reduced undertriage from 21% to 11% and overtriage from 63% to 57%. Even with this improvement, both rates remained high, and the physician-staffed call model doesn't match how Australian dispatch works.

questions.short_title: Reported LOC didn't flag post-traumatic amnesia in ED
questions.question: In this Australian ED cohort of adults tested with the A-WPTAS after head injury, how did pass rates relate to documented loss of consciousness?
options: LOC predicted failure only in patients with GCS 15
Pass rates were similar with and without documented LOC
Pass rates were clearly lower in patients with documented LOC
Only patients with LOC failed the A-WPTAS
questions.explanation: Pass rates were 90.6% with documented LOC and 92% without, a difference that wasn't statistically significant. PTA on the scale lined up with GCS 13-14 instead, though the study was retrospective, ED-only, and didn't link back to prehospital documentation.

questions.short_title: Predicting ground vs helicopter EMS travel times
questions.question: When comparing the predictive models, which travel times were hardest to estimate accurately?
options: Ground EMS transport times to hospital
Ground EMS drive times to the scene
Helicopter flight times
Both were predicted with similar accuracy
questions.explanation: Helicopter flight times had the weakest models (R² 0.46 and 0.38 versus 0.79 and 0.70 for ground), so their times are much less predictable. Accuracy also depends on local geography and data quality.

questions.short_title: Mapping anti-violence measures for ambulance personnel
questions.question: This review will classify anti-violence measures using several conceptual frameworks. Which one is included?
options: Crime prevention through environmental design
Trauma-informed care principles
Root cause analysis and just culture
Levels of prevention and hierarchy of controls
questions.explanation: The protocol maps measures across five frameworks including levels of prevention and the hierarchy of controls. It's only a protocol with no results yet, so it offers context rather than findings, and the single-reviewer title/abstract screening is a limitation.
